title: Point Roberts
hook: A corner of Washington State you can only drive to through Canada.
peek: Point Roberts is a small tip of land below the 49th parallel, joined to Canada and cut off from the rest of the US by water. Older children ride a bus through two border crossings each way to reach school.
lede: In 1846 Britain and the United States agreed to split the land along the 49th parallel. Nobody noticed that the line clipped the end of a peninsula south of what is now Vancouver. That tip, about 13 square kilometres, became Point Roberts, Washington. By land it touches only Canada, and the nearest US town by road is about 40 kilometres away.

bullets.text: Point Roberts has a small primary school for its youngest pupils. Older students ride a bus to Blaine, Washington, crossing into Canada and back into the US each way, so four border crossings a day.
The town has no big water source of its own, so most of its water is piped in from Greater Vancouver. Many of its homes also belong to Canadians who come down for the summer.
The only routes that avoid Canada are by water or air. Across Boundary Bay, the rest of Washington is visible from the beach on a clear day.
